title: split-state-and-gpu-pool-modules-enable-taints-node-affinity-terraform
author: Priya Malhotra
release_notes: Introduce modular GPU node pools and IAM instance profile modules for Private deployments. Add a split backend/state layout per-environment and per-nodepool to improve parallelism and reduce plan conflicts. Provide migration helper and rollback guidance. No user-facing API changes; infra-only.
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require tighter isolation between GPU node pools, network configuration, and Terraform state to support per-customer upgrades, safe rollbacks, and parallel apply workflows. Currently we keep a single, monolithic state per-cluster which causes long locks during upgrades and makes targeted rollbacks risky. This PR refactors the Terraform layout and introduces two new reusable modules (gpu_node_pool and iam_instance_profile), moves to a split-state layout, and wires minimal networking changes required for customer VPC topologies.

What this PR does (summary):
- Extract modules/gpu_node_pool: encapsulates node pool sizing, autoscaling policies, GPU taints, node-affinity labels, and kubelet config overrides.
- Add modules/iam_instance_profile: creates least-privilege instance roles and instance profiles for GPU nodes (SSM, CloudWatch, limited S3 for telemetry upload), with an optional external id for cross-account/private setups.
- Update modules/networking to support per-nodepool route tables and optional private subnet tagging for on-prem-style NAT routing.
- Move remote state to env-scoped backends with an additional nodepool-scoped backend option. Defaults keep backward compatibility by mapping old backend when migrating.
- Add scripts/migrate-state.sh: automated helpers to split state via terraform state mv, with dry-run mode and logging.
- Add example private/gpu-cluster.tf and testing harness to run a zero-downtime canary apply against staging.

Why this layout: The split-state approach reduces contention for long-running operations (e.g., draining/replacing GPU pools), enables targeted rollouts (canary one nodepool), and makes incremental restores/rollbacks possible by isolating state for critical components. The IAM module centralizes least-privilege concerns for audits and future RBAC automation.

Migration notes (high-level):
1) Run terraform init against the existing env backend and review current state.
2) Use scripts/migrate-state.sh --dry-run to get a mapping plan; confirm the plan in Linear ENG-1274.
3) For each nodepool to split out: terraform state mv <old_resource> <new_module_address> and verify with terraform plan.
4) Apply nodepool backends independently. For customers with strict change windows, plan/approve each nodepool apply.

Rollback guidance: Keep old backend snapshots (we retain S3 versioning and a timestamped lock) and use terraform state mv to recompose the original state if a rollback is needed. The script includes an --undo mapping file.

Testing performed:
- Staging deployment (private-eu-stg) exercised a full canary: created a new GPU node pool (nvidia-a100) with taints and node-affinity for inference workload; drained one old nodepool and validated k8s pod disruption budgets and service availability.
- IAM role checks: Verified instance profile attaches only required policies (CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy, SSMManagedInstanceCore + scoped S3 putObject to telemetry bucket).
- CI: terraform init/validate/plan/fmt/lint passed after one fmt fix; e2e canary apply executed against staging and smoke tests passed.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Module extraction and unit tests for tf modules
- [x] Migration script with dry-run and logging
- [x] Example for customer-private VPC topology
- [x] Security review: least-privilege IAM defaults
- [x] Performance test: reduced plan lock contention in staging

Notes and tradeoffs:
- This introduces more Terraform state files to manage; operational complexity increases but enables parallelism and safer rollouts. We provide automation to mitigate human error.
- Nodepool-level state means cross-resource references must use data sources or remote_state outputs; we add output contracts in modules to make this explicit.

Related: ENG-1274 (split TF state for private), ENG-1389 (gpu autoscale improvements).

review_thread: Anita Rao (2026-02-23): Can you justify exposing external_id in the IAM module? We need it for cross-account installs but must ensure it's optional and never required by default.
Priya Malhotra (2026-02-23): Good catch — external_id is optional and documented. Default is null; module will only create a condition when set. Added tests to verify behavior.
Liam Chen (2026-02-25): Request changes: the node affinity logic needs an explicit topologyKey for multi-az clusters, and please add acceptance checks for scheduling (PDB respects during drain).

Priya Malhotra (2026-02-26): Addressed: added topology_key var with default "topology.kubernetes.io/zone" and added a staging acceptance test that simulates drain and validates PDB and readiness gates.
Marcus Vega (2026-03-01): Approved after LGTMs and CI green. Verified that the state migration script has a dry-run and undo path.

notes_for_release_engineering: This changes Terraform state layout for private clusters. Before rolling to production customers, coordinate a migration window. Use scripts/migrate-state.sh in dry-run mode to generate state move commands; confirm S3 backend versioning is enabled. No helm changes included here; helm chart teams should be informed when nodepool names or labels change.
post_merge_actions: Schedule rolling canary for production tenant with dedicated maintenance window
Document new module contracts in terraform registry and examples
